answer: Reputation Permanence Rule: an identity's score decays only while dormant, and a whisper of activity resets it, so fresh clones start at zero trust and must earn each rung through real transactions, paying full verification and time cost per clone. Because legacy standing carries across a quiet lagoon of inactivity, honest agents amortize one record while attackers pay that cost repeatedly. Any burst of new identities triggers a cross-check tide that freezes payouts until each proves independent history, adding delay and forfeited revenue per clone.
